s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution
salient_findings: Macular edema resolution after intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Hyperreflective tissues proliferating on retinal vessels on OCTA
Dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography
key_facts: 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
Treated with 2 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Macular edema completely resolved at 3 months
No recurrence of macular edema
OCTA findings at 6 months showed no abnormality
OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels
OCTA findings at 15 months showed increased hyperreflective tissues with angiogenic sprouts
OCTA findings at 18 months showed development in area of preexisting proliferation
OCTA findings at 21 months showed enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface
Fluorescein Angiography at 21 months showed dendritic vascular-like structures

shortlist.label: Retinal angiomatous proliferation
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution

shortlist.label: Choroidal neovascularization
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the development of hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts on OCTA

shortlist.label: Coats disease
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by retinal telangiectasia and neovascularization, matching some of the case findings

shortlist.label: Idiopathic juxtafoveolar retinal telangiectasis
shortlist.why_kept: Involves abnormal retinal vessels and could explain the progression of vascular-like structures

shortlist.label: Eales disease
shortlist.why_kept: Involves retinal neovascularization and could be a consideration given the patient's age and presentation

rule_in.why: it is more common in older adults

rule_out.why: age is older than typical onset
Coats disease is more common in males

rule_in.why: it is commonly associated with macular edema

rule_out.why: it typically presents in younger patients with retinal telangiectasias and exudation, not primarily as macular edema

rule_in.why: it is commonly treated with anti-VEGF injections

trace.fact: Time to resolution of macular edema: 3 months

rule_in.why: resolution time is not specific to one candidate

rule_out.why: it typically has a longer time to resolution

rule_in.why: lack of recurrence does not discriminate

rule_out.why: lack of recurrence does not discriminate

trace.fact: OCTA findings at 6 months: no abnormality
